verdict.rationale: Unity publishes an explicit API lifecycle policy for its Services Web APIs. Endpoints are path-versioned, breaking changes go only into new versions, and deprecated versions get three months to a year of continued support plus at least two months' shutdown notice. The versioned OpenAPI spec catalog (e.g. Cloud Save 1.0.0) corroborates the versioning. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the policy is honored, a documented deprecation policy beyond the Services Web APIs (e.g. engine/editor scripting APIs), and a support window comparable to the 12-24 month commitments of other cloud vendors.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: The API may receive non-breaking changes without its version number being changed. Breaking changes are introduced only to new API versions.

After three months to a year of continued support for a deprecated version, Unity may cease support or shutdown that version entirely. A version shutdown notice will be posted in this portal at least 2 months in advance.
Unity publishes downloadable OpenAPI documents for its Services Web APIs
